<reason>B won the live decision rule: the motion’s “even if,” not a peat-fire ban with extra adjectives. A’s deletion-vs-debt frame and 2015 haze were the stronger constructive, but they never fully mapped illegal burning onto lawful frontier hectares. B split those harms, forced A to name legal losers and keep the cut if the grant never comes, and left a cleaner ballot line: close the canal; do not bill school fees for a fire the child did not set. A’s early rename and B’s clipped R1 kept it competitive, not a blowout.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Q1 plus R2: spare legal planters and you abandon the “even if”; A then named undeveloped concessions/frontier plots and said the rule stands without compensation—B used that as the closing lock.</best_rebuttal>
